best_immediately_usable_next_edit_corpus.language_provenance: TypeScript is the original data. Python, C, Rust, and Java variants were synthetically translated from the TypeScript examples with a self-hosted code model.
limits: The original edits come from one product team and their open-source work, not a broad sample of developers.
The training examples are filtered edit chunks, not a raw keypress/cursor/session trace.
The card lists messages but no author/session grouping field; check the actual train rows for reliable group identifiers before deriving train/dev examples.
This corpus was not downloaded or added to current training data during this audit.
best_immediately_usable_next_edit_corpus.name: Continue Instinct data
best_immediately_usable_next_edit_corpus.recommended_use: If selected later, pin this revision, prepare only official train splits, keep every official test split sealed, and audit cross-language/source-example duplication before assigning any additional validation split.
best_immediately_usable_next_edit_corpus.signal: The authors describe over 4,000 real edits collected from the Continue team. They chunked edits with line- and timing-based rules, and examples carry recent edit history, context, editable region, and target change.

best_real_developer_edit_data_if_access_.access: Gated. The card requires manual approval and contact details, limits use to research, requires privacy protection, and prohibits re-identification.
best_real_developer_edit_data_if_access_.current_audit_action: No request, download, or use. Approval is not available in this audit.
best_real_developer_edit_data_if_access_.handling_if_approved: Group all rows from a user and completion trajectory together; order only by recorded edit timestamps; reserve complete users or trajectories for evaluation; do not infer keypresses or cursor events from snapshots.
best_real_developer_edit_data_if_access_.license_status: No standard open-source or Creative Commons license is visible on the access-gated card. Review the approved terms before any use.
best_real_developer_edit_data_if_access_.name: DECODE: Developer Edits of Code Dataset
best_real_developer_edit_data_if_access_.signal: Observed in-IDE snapshots of edits to accepted AI completions; the card lists user IDs, completion/edit IDs, timestamps, and before/after code fields.

limits: A Git commit records a submitted final change, not intermediate edits or cursor order.
Commit timestamps describe version-control metadata, not necessarily when the code was edited.
Multi-file commits can combine unrelated intent; merges, bots, copied patches, and squash commits need explicit handling.
A patch diff alone does not reveal why the author made the change or whether they later reverted it.
Do not label commit-derived pairs as real-time developer next-edit trajectories.
commit_derived_edit_pairs.recipe: For exact-pinned permissively licensed repositories, reconstruct single-parent commit transitions from parent tree to commit tree; retain source license and commit/repository identity per example.
commit_derived_edit_pairs.split_policy: For repository-generalization claims, split whole repositories. For within-repository chronological prediction, train only on earlier commits and evaluate on later commits, while keeping all files/near-duplicate examples from a commit together.
commit_derived_edit_pairs.status: Useful scale-up proxy, but not observed editing traces.

small_real_trace_for_replay_and_edit_mec.license: CC-BY-4.0, as stated for rustcode and sveltecomponent in the pinned README
limits: Both files are attributed to Joseph Gentle, so they cannot support an author-held-out claim.
The Rust trace starts after much of its code was written; its first transaction inserts 42,493 codepoints.
The first Svelte transaction inserts 1,406 codepoints.
Each file has one 1970-01-01T00:00:00.000Z transaction time value with undocumented meaning.
Transaction timestamps have second-level precision and ties occur, so input order is the only within-time ordering evidence.
Patches do not encode explicit cursor selection, undo/redo, acceptance, or intent labels.
small_real_trace_for_replay_and_edit_mec.name: josephg/editing-traces sequential Rust and Svelte traces
small_real_trace_for_replay_and_edit_mec.recommended_use: Keep as a small parser/replay fixture or separate qualitative trace set. Do not use it as a representative split or broad next-edit training bank.
small_real_trace_for_replay_and_edit_mec.signal: Real ordered text-edit transactions captured with a VS Code tracker, suitable for validating Unicode-offset replay and transaction handling.
